paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: this passage is about turning to the wrong place when the right place is standing right there. Ephraim ran to Egypt, then to Assyria, like a "silly, senseless dove" (Hosea 7:11). And the whole time, the LORD says, "Though I would redeem them…" (Hosea 7:13). The One who wanted to rescue them was the one they kept flapping away from.

Look at what keeps going wrong. Their strength was draining and "he does not notice" (Hosea 7:9). They did not "return to the LORD their God" (Hosea 7:10), and they did not cry out to Him "from their hearts" (Hosea 7:14). I think the scary part isn't one big disaster, it's the slow drift where nobody checks the timer. Baker, I've left a batch in too long while I was busy looking at something else, and the oven did not wait for me to notice.

So here's what to carry out of my bakery today. The LORD trained and strengthened their arms (Hosea 7:15), so everything good they had came from Him, and that's a reason to turn back to Him and not to a backup plan. Check where you run first when things get shaky. Turn to the Most High, because He is the only One who will never be a faulty bow.
